verses.sa: अश्वत्थः सर्ववृक्षाणां देवर्षीणां च नारदः । गन्धर्वाणां चित्ररथः सिद्धानां कपिलो मुनिः ॥
verses.tr: Among all trees I am the sacred fig tree. Among divine sages I am Narada; among celestial musicians, Chitraratha; among perfected sages, the sage Kapila.
verses.angle: Krishna pairs the best of each group
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna continues his list of the finest forms. Listen for how he pairs the greatest among trees and sages with the best among musicians and perfected beings.

body.text: Among all trees I am the sacred fig tree. Among divine sages I am Narada; among celestial musicians, Chitraratha; among perfected sages, the sage Kapila. Krishna pairs the greatest among trees with the greatest among divine sages, and the best among musicians with the best among perfected sages, showing a pattern of the highest in every category. He now turns to horses, elephants, and kings, naming the lord of horses born from nectar.

verses.sa: उच्चैःश्रवसमश्वानां विद्धि माममृतोद्भवम् । ऐरावतं गजेन्द्राणां नराणां च नराधिपम् ॥
verses.tr: Among horses, know me as Ucchaihshravas, born from nectar. Among royal elephants, I am Airavata, and among humans, I am the king.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: A question hangs over the chapter: how can the infinite be seen in the world around us? Krishna answers by naming the greatest of every kind.

body.text: Among horses, know me as Ucchaihshravas, born from nectar. Among royal elephants, I am Airavata, and among humans, I am the king. Ucchaihshravas the horse was born from the churning of the ocean, and Airavata the elephant emerged from the same waters, yet both are only one among many, while the king stands above the rest of humanity. Krishna now names the greatest weapons and the king of serpents, the thunderbolt and Vasuki.

verses.sa: आयुधानामहं वज्रं धेनूनामस्मि कामधुक् । प्रजनश्चास्मि कन्दर्पः सर्पाणामस्मि वासुकिः ॥
verses.tr: Among weapons, I am the thunderbolt; among cows, I am the wish-fulfilling cow. I am the cause of procreation, and among serpents, I am Vasuki.
verses.angle: Desire is one of Krishna's divine forms
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: The battlefield of Kurukshetra is a stage for the divine. Listen to how Krishna names his presence in the very forces of creation.

body.text: Among weapons, I am the thunderbolt; among cows, I am the wish-fulfilling cow. I am the cause of procreation, and among serpents, I am Vasuki. Notice how Krishna includes the wish-fulfilling cow and the force of procreation in his list, placing desire itself among his divine forms. Krishna continues naming the highest beings in creation, moving from Vasuki to Varuna, the lord of the waters.

verses.sa: अनन्तश्चास्मि नागानां वरुणो यादसामहम् । पितृ़णामर्यमा चास्मि यमः संयमतामहम् ॥
verses.tr: Among serpents I am Ananta; among water beings I am Varuna. Among ancestors I am Aryaman; among those who govern, I am Yama.
verses.angle: Asmi: I am present in all beings
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna is naming his own presence inside every part of the world. Listen for the word that repeats after each being he names.

body.text: Among serpents I am Ananta; among water beings I am Varuna. Among ancestors I am Aryaman; among those who govern, I am Yama. The word is asmi, I am. Krishna says he is these beings. The one presence fills the serpent, the water, the ancestors, and the judge of the dead. Krishna then names Prahlada and the lion, moving from a devotee to a wild beast.

verses.sa: प्रह्लादश्चास्मि दैत्यानां कालः कलयतामहम् । मृगाणां च मृगेन्द्रोऽहं वैनतेयश्च पक्षिणाम् ॥
verses.tr: Among the daityas I am Prahlada; among calculators I am Time. Among beasts I am the lion, and among birds I am Garuda.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has been naming his presence in the world, and now he moves from the cosmic to the personal. Hear how he claims to be Prahlada.

body.text: Among the daityas I am Prahlada; among calculators I am Time. Among beasts I am the lion, and among birds I am Garuda. Listen to the first name Krishna gives here, Prahlada. He is the daitya prince whose devotion outshone his demon father, and Krishna says he is that very devotion among the demons. Krishna then names Time, the lion, and Garuda, showing that absolute power and speed are also his.

verses.sa: पवनः पवतामस्मि रामः शस्त्रभृतामहम् । झषाणां मकरश्चास्मि स्रोतसामस्मि जाह्नवी ॥
verses.tr: Among purifiers, I am the wind. Among wielders of weapons, I am Rama. Among aquatic beings, I am the crocodile. Among flowing rivers, I am the Ganga.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna carries on by naming the supreme of each class. Listen to the four figures he claims as his own.

body.text: Among purifiers, I am the wind. Among wielders of weapons, I am Rama. Among aquatic beings, I am the crocodile. Among flowing rivers, I am the Ganga. Listen to the crocodile. It is the fiercest creature of the water, and Krishna places it among the aquatic beings, showing his presence in the most fearsome form of the wild. Krishna now claims the beginning, the middle, and the end of all creation, and the knowledge of the true self. Listen to how he names his own limits.

verses.sa: सर्गाणामादिरन्तश्च मध्यं चैवाहमर्जुन । अध्यात्मविद्या विद्यानां वादः प्रवदतामहम् ॥
verses.tr: I am the beginning, the middle, and the end of all creation, Arjuna. Among all forms of knowledge, I am the knowledge of the true self; among speakers, I am the reasoned debate that seeks truth.
verses.angle: The knowledge of the self and the debate that seeks it
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just listed many visible forms of his power. Now he names the invisible forces that hold knowledge and argument together. Listen for how he places them.

body.text: I am the beginning, the middle, and the end of all creation, Arjuna. Among all forms of knowledge, I am the knowledge of the true self; among speakers, I am the reasoned debate that seeks truth. Krishna says he is the knowledge of the true self among all sciences, and the reasoned debate among speakers. He places the inner truth and the spoken argument on equal ground. He now moves from knowledge to the very letters and time that build it.

verses.sa: अक्षराणामकारोऽस्मि द्वन्द्वः सामासिकस्य च । अहमेवाक्षयः कालो धाताऽहं विश्वतोमुखः ॥
verses.tr: Among letters I am the letter A. Among compounds I am the dual compound. I am endless time itself, and I am the all-facing sustainer.
verses.angle: Ahameva: the first syllable of the imperishable
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna shifts from forms of knowledge to the grammar of the universe. Listen for the first letter and the first compound.

body.text: Among letters I am the letter A. Among compounds I am the dual compound. I am endless time itself, and I am the all-facing sustainer. The word ahameva, I indeed, stands alone. It is the first syllable of the word akshara, the imperishable. Here, the speaker claims to be the very first letter of the alphabet and the endless time that follows. Krishna moves from the grammar of language to the grammar of life, naming the women who shape human destiny.

verses.sa: मृत्युः सर्वहरश्चाहमुद्भवश्च भविष्यताम् । कीर्तिः श्रीर्वाक्च नारीणां स्मृतिर्मेधा धृतिः क्षमा ॥
verses.tr: I am death that takes everything, and the source of all future beings. Among women, I am fame, fortune, speech, memory, intelligence, steadfastness, and forgiveness.
verses.angle: Death and birth: the two forces of existence
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has named cosmic powers, letters, and time. Now he names the forces that shape human life itself. Listen for the two words that mark the end and the start of all beings.

body.text: I am death that takes everything, and the source of all future beings. Among women, I am fame, fortune, speech, memory, intelligence, steadfastness, and forgiveness. The word mrityuh, death, is paired with sarvaharah, all-taking. Together they describe the force that ends every life, and the word udbhava, origin, names the force that starts all future beings. Krishna now moves to the qualities that make human life dignified, naming seven virtues among women.

verses.sa: बृहत्साम तथा साम्नां गायत्री छन्दसामहम् । मासानां मार्गशीर्षोऽहमृतूनां कुसुमाकरः ॥
verses.tr: Among hymns I am the Brihat-Sama; among meters I am Gayatri. Among months I am Margashirsha; among seasons I am spring.
verses.angle: Krishna in the calendar of time
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna continues to show Arjuna where he is found, moving from human qualities to the very order of time itself. Listen for the sacred sounds and the turning of the seasons.

body.text: Among hymns I am the Brihat-Sama; among meters I am Gayatri. Among months I am Margashirsha; among seasons I am spring. Krishna sits inside the calendar itself. He is the Gayatri among meters, the month of Margashirsha among months, and spring among seasons. Nothing is outside him. Krishna then names his presence in the midst of those who deceive, showing he is found even in human cunning.

verses.sa: द्यूतं छलयतामस्मि तेजस्तेजस्विनामहम् । जयोऽस्मि व्यवसायोऽस्मि सत्त्वं सत्त्ववतामहम् ॥
verses.tr: Among deceivers I am gambling, among the vigorous I am splendor. I am victory, I am resolve, and I am the goodness of the good.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna keeps naming where divine power appears, even in the ordinary. Listen for the surprising place he places himself.

body.text: Among deceivers I am gambling, among the vigorous I am splendor. I am victory, I am resolve, and I am the goodness of the good. The word dutyam, gambling, belongs to the deceivers, yet Krishna claims it as his own form. Victory, resolve, and noble character are all his expressions. He then names Vasudeva among the Vrishnis and Dhananjaya among the Pandavas.

verses.sa: वृष्णीनां वासुदेवोऽस्मि पाण्डवानां धनंजयः । मुनीनामप्यहं व्यासः कवीनामुशना कविः ॥
verses.tr: Among the Vrishnis I am Vasudeva; among the Pandavas I am Dhananjaya. Among sages I am Vyasa, and among poets I am Ushana, the poet.
verses.angle: Krishna names his greatest human manifestations
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna lists the greatest among the Vrishnis, the Pandavas, the sages, and the poets. Listen to how he places his presence at the heart of human excellence.

body.text: Among the Vrishnis I am Vasudeva; among the Pandavas I am Dhananjaya. Among sages I am Vyasa, and among poets I am Ushana, the poet. Krishna names himself as the greatest among the Vrishnis, the Pandavas, the sages, and the poets. He places his own divine presence at the heart of human excellence, from the mightiest warrior to the wisest sage. Krishna continues naming his presence among enforcers, seekers, and secrets.

verses.sa: दण्डो दमयतामस्मि नीतिरस्मि जिगीषताम् । मौनं चैवास्मि गुह्यानां ज्ञानं ज्ञानवतामहम् ॥
verses.tr: Among enforcers, I am punishment; among those seeking victory, I am policy. Among secrets, I am silence; among the wise, I am knowledge.
verses.angle: Silence and knowledge as forms of power
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna lists the quiet tools of governing and the force behind them. Listen to how he places silence and knowledge alongside punishment and policy.

body.text: Among enforcers, I am punishment; among those seeking victory, I am policy. Among secrets, I am silence; among the wise, I am knowledge. Krishna claims four forms of his presence: corrective force, strategic conduct, silence, and the knowledge of the wise. He then moves from governing to creation, declaring he is the seed of all beings.

verses.sa: यच्चापि सर्वभूतानां बीजं तदहमर्जुन । न तदस्ति विना यत्स्यान्मया भूतं चराचरम् ॥
verses.tr: Arjuna, I am the seed of all beings. Without me, nothing moving or unmoving could exist.
verses.angle: Bija, the seed of all beings
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just named his many forms and powers. Now he points to the single source behind all of them. Listen for the word he uses for that origin.

body.text: Arjuna, I am the seed of all beings. Without me, nothing moving or unmoving could exist. Krishna says he is the bija, the seed, of all beings. Without this seed, nothing that moves or stands still could exist. It is the foundation of all that is. He then says his forms are endless and what he has shared is only a small part of his divine presence.

verses.sa: नान्तोऽस्ति मम दिव्यानां विभूतीनां परंतप । एष तूद्देशतः प्रोक्तो विभूतेर्विस्तरो मया ॥
verses.tr: O scorcher of foes, my divine manifestations have no end. What I have described to you is only a brief summary of my vast manifestations.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just finished listing many of his divine forms, and now he speaks directly to Arjuna about the limits of that list.

body.text: O scorcher of foes, my divine manifestations have no end. What I have described to you is only a brief summary of my vast manifestations. Krishna admits that his divine manifestations have no end, and the examples he just gave are only a brief summary. He now tells Arjuna to know that every splendid thing arises from a spark of his own radiance.

verses.sa: यद्यद्विभूतिमत्सत्त्वं श्रीमदूर्जितमेव वा । तत्तदेवावगच्छ त्वं मम तेजोंऽशसंभवम् ॥
verses.tr: Whatever being or thing is endowed with splendour, beauty, or power, know that to have arisen from a spark of my radiance.
verses.angle: Every splendor is a spark of Krishna
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just said his manifestations are endless, yet now he pulls the point tight. Listen for the single source he names.

body.text: Whatever being or thing is endowed with splendour, beauty, or power, know that to have arisen from a spark of my radiance. Krishna tells Arjuna that every grand, strong, or glorious thing is only a portion of his radiance. He then steps back from the list and asks if Arjuna really needs to know every detail.

verses.sa: अथवा बहुनैतेन किं ज्ञातेन तवार्जुन । विष्टभ्याहमिदं कृत्स्नमेकांशेन स्थितो जगत् ॥
verses.tr: Or, Arjuna, what is the need for all this detailed knowledge? I sustain this entire universe with a single fragment of myself.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just shown Arjuna endless divine forms. Now he asks what use there is in knowing all of them. Listen to his answer.

body.text: Or, Arjuna, what is the need for all this detailed knowledge? I sustain this entire universe with a single fragment of myself. The word to notice is ekamsena, a single part. Krishna says that even one fragment of his presence is enough to sustain the whole universe. Arjuna accepts this truth and asks to see the universal form.

next.title: Arjuna asks to see the cosmic form
